questions.q: Why is a "happy path only" integration script considered incomplete by design, not just unfinished?
options: Because REST Message records cannot be tested until error handling exists
Because the external system it depends on will eventually go down, expire its credentials, change its schema, or rate-limit it, and none of those are coding bugs
Because happy-path code always runs slower than code with error handling
Because ServiceNow refuses to run scripts that lack a try/catch block
questions.explain: A happy-path-only script has simply never had its failure modes considered — those failures are the normal operating condition of a dependency you don't control.

questions.q: Look at this code: `var response = request.execute(); var data = JSON.parse(response.getBody());`. What does this code silently assume?
options: That the external system requires no Authentication Profile
That the REST Message record has already been deleted
That JSON.parse() always throws an exception on success
That the call returned HTTP 200 with valid JSON in the shape the script expects
questions.explain: There's no status-code check and no try/catch around the parse — the code assumes success and a stable response shape.

questions.q: What does an external system returning HTTP 429 actually mean?
options: The caller exceeded an allowed call volume, and the system is protecting itself, not reporting an outage
The requested resource does not exist on the external system
The external system has a schema mismatch with the request body
The caller's OAuth token has expired
questions.explain: 429 Too Many Requests is rate limiting — the system is healthy but asking the caller to slow down, which calls for backing off rather than retrying immediately.

questions.q: What can happen inside ServiceNow if a business rule's script throws an exception that is never caught?
options: Nothing happens; unhandled exceptions have no effect in ServiceNow scripts
The transaction the business rule ran in can be aborted, with no explicit record of why unless someone finds it in logs later
ServiceNow automatically retries the exact same operation three times with no code change needed
The platform silently converts the exception into a successful HTTP 200 response
questions.explain: An unhandled exception can abort the surrounding transaction or flow run, leaving the failure to be discovered later rather than handled at the moment it happened.

questions.q: Per this lesson's design principle, why is it usually pointless to immediately retry a request that got back an HTTP 4xx client error?
options: Because 4xx errors always resolve themselves within one second
Because a 4xx means the request itself is malformed or unauthorized, so repeating it unchanged just repeats the same failure
Because retrying a 4xx permanently bans the integration user's account
Because 4xx errors can only happen on GET requests, never on POST
questions.explain: A 4xx points to a problem with the request itself (bad auth, bad input) — retrying the same bad request produces the same bad result.
